text:
Ava (Support): hi team — customer reported a wave of 413s when uploading very large embedding batches via our embeddings endpoint. They say they switched to a chunked/streaming upload to avoid a single massive JSON array but still see Payload Too Large from our edge. stack: node client -> nginx proxy -> redwood-api (hosted).

Kai (ML Eng): can you paste the failing request example + headers? 413 usually means an upstream/edge limit (nginx, load balancer) or we still validate full size before accepting chunked streams.

Ava (Support): here's the anonymized curl they sent, they used Transfer-Encoding: chunked and NDJSON (one vector per line):

```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/stream \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" \n  --data-binary @vectors.ndjson
```

vectors.ndjson looked like: 1k-10k lines, each line JSON: `{"id": "doc-123", "vector": [0.12, -0.33, ...]}`. They said each vector is dim=1536 and the file ~120MB. First request attempt returned 413 immediately.

Samir (Devops): nginx default client_max_body_size is 1m on some proxies; but they said they used chunked so Content-Length shouldn't matter. Do we do any pre-validation in the control plane that buffers the whole request? Could be our API gateway buffering before we stream to the embed service. I'll check the proxy configs.

ingest-bot: auto-ticket created INC-9876 for high-volume embedding 413s (owner: ingest-team).

Kai (ML Eng): two separate angles: 1) dimension mismatch errors we've seen when users accidentally mix models (1024 vs 1536); 2) throughput + request size limits. If the embed model expects 1536 dims but some lines shorter/longer we might return a 422 or 400 — not 413 — so this is probably size. But confirm logs for 422/400 in the same timeframe.

Ava (Support): customer also reported intermittent dimension warnings earlier in a different run: `dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024` for ~20 lines and they filtered those out before reuploading. The 413s started after they retried with the filtered file.

Renee (Platform): quick summary of our current constraints (internal):
- edge LB (nginx) configured with client_max_body_size = 32M in eu region, 10M in us-west.
- platform API gateway will buffer up to 8M before switching to streaming path; above that it rejects.
- streaming endpoint /v1/embeddings/stream is supported but only for chunked NDJSON up to 100MB total if routed to dedicated ingest nodes; otherwise falls back and hits buffer limits.

Samir (Devops): log snippet from the router during the customer's window: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/embeddings/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.10.10.11:8080/"` then nginx responded 413. Looks like the gateway aborted. I think gateway validation tries to peek first N bytes to determine content-type and then enforces a hard size limit.

Kai (ML Eng): practical troubleshooting steps we gave the customer: 1) reduce per-request batch size to 1k vectors (roughly 12MB for 1536-d float32 JSON), 2) compress payloads (gzip) and set `Content-Encoding: gzip` — our gateway supports it and gzip often reduces JSON ~3-6x, 3) use model-specific dimensions: ensure vectors are float32 arrays with length 1536 for embed-large-v2, 4) if using chunked streaming, ensure each NDJSON line is valid and not sending a trailing comma/array wrapper.

Ava (Support): customer tried splitting to 2k vector batches and the 413s stopped — per their report, successful. They asked if we can increase limits so they can upload whole dataset in fewer requests.

Renee (Platform): short-term doc/update: recommend clients cap JSON payloads to 8–12MB per request for hosted API. Long-term: platform team is evaluating dynamic routing so big streaming uploads are routed to ingest nodes without going through the buffer-heavy gateway. ETA TBD. We'll create a public doc with guidance + example streaming patterns.

Samir (Devops): I pushed a quick config change to the test LB to allow 64M in a canary pool and routed one of the ingest nodes through it. Ran an internal test with a 60MB NDJSON file (1536 dims, ~5k vectors) and the streaming path accepted it without 413. Need to run a soak test before we change prod.

Kai (ML Eng): note on memory: when customers send giant JSON arrays, our model workers may need to materialize vectors in memory — recommend streaming NDJSON with per-line validation so we can process in chunks and avoid OOM on workers. That requires the full request to reach the streaming router rather than being pre-buffered.

Ava (Support): customer follow-up: they accepted the 1k batch workaround and gzip suggestion for now. They asked: could we return a more helpful error than 413 pointing them to size docs? (they initially thought 413 meant auth).

Renee (Platform): agree — we should change our 413 response body for embeddings endpoints to include: "payload too large: try batching <= 12MB, or use gzip and Transfer-Encoding: chunked; contact support for ingest routing". I'll file a docs + response improvement ticket.

ingest-bot: linked INC-9876 -> DOCS-453 (add streaming/batching guidance).

Ava (Support): final notes for thread: assigned to platform (Renee) to track canary -> prod change, kai to review binary multipart proposal, samir to run soak tests. I'll close the support case once platform confirms ETA. Thanks all :thumbsup: :eyes: 

Samir (Devops): I'll post canary metrics in #eng-infra once soak completes, ETA 48h.

Kai (ML Eng): also adding a short example to the support playbook for dimension mismatch detection + remediation commands (python snippet to validate vector dims locally).

Ava (Support): thanks — marking as resolved on the customer side, keeping INC-9876 open for platform action.

billing-bot: note: no billing anomalies detected for this customer during window.

Ava (Support): closing thread — will follow up on DOCS-453 updates.
